- Open the switcher on the display of the focused window, with even spacing around every icon.
- Move windows only to the display directly beside, above, or below in the direction you press.
- Return to the app you just left when switching from Ruf Settings or switching twice in quick succession.
- Match switcher shortcuts by the letter you type, so other keyboard layouts no longer quit or open windows by key position.
- Keep held Return, Escape, and Tab keys from repeating into the app you switch to.
- Show every instance of an app, and apps without a bundle identifier.
- Include helper processes such as Safari's web content in an app's CPU and memory usage.
- Open one window instead of two when New Window is slow to respond.
- Show available updates in Ruf's menu and switcher instead of an alert behind other apps.
- Open Settings on the display you are working on, and keep every switcher row on screen when many apps are open.
